# Day

> Day builds native desktop and mobile apps from shared Rust code. Pieces describe the interface;
> each backend creates controls through its platform’s UI toolkit. Signals update the controls
> that depend on them. Structural changes can create or remove subtrees.

This file follows the llmstxt.org convention. The page at /docs/reference/for-agents is written specifically for
AI agents (dense, rule-based, canonical); start there if you are generating Day code.

## Quick facts

- Language: Rust. Import everything with `use day::prelude::*;`.
- Naming: **Day** = the framework (capitalized). `day` = the CLI binary and the crate (lowercase).
- A UI node is a **Piece**; state is a `Copy` reactive **Signal<T>**; a **target** is an `(OS, toolkit)`
  pair (e.g. `macos-appkit`, `ios-uikit`, `android-mdc`, `linux-gtk`, `windows-winui`).
- Reactivity: static content passes a value (`label("Hi")`); dynamic content passes a closure that
  reads a Signal (`label(move || n.get().to_string())`). Only bindings that read a changed Signal re-run.
- One toolkit backend is compiled per binary (selected by the target); enabling two is a `compile_error!`.
- CLI: `day new` (interactive scaffold; `day new app|piece|part <name> …` non-interactive) · `day build
  -t <target>` · `day launch -t <target>` · `day launch -t <target> --script <s.yaml>` (drive/assert a
  running app) · `day pack` · `day lint` · `day doctor`.
- Give any Piece a stable `.id(id!(control_name))` so dayscript, tests, and deep links can address it.

## Docs

- [For AI Agents](https://daybrite.dev/docs/reference/for-agents): dense, canonical, rule-based reference for LLMs — invariants, canonical patterns, API cheat-sheet, failure modes.
- [Overview](https://daybrite.dev/docs/explanation/overview): what Day is, how it works, the targets it ships.
- [Why Day](https://daybrite.dev/features): the case for native widgets + build-once/bind-forever.
- [API tour](https://daybrite.dev/docs/reference/api-tour): Pieces, Signals, layout, inputs, navigation, localization, accessibility, extensibility — with runnable snippets.
- [CLI & projects](https://daybrite.dev/docs/reference/cli): the `day` CLI, the conventional project layout, `Day.toml`, and dayscript automation.

## Documentation by task

Canonical app documentation is grouped by purpose:

- [Tutorials](https://daybrite.dev/docs/tutorials): guided learning.
- [How-to guides](https://daybrite.dev/docs/how-to): specific tasks.
- [Reference](https://daybrite.dev/docs/reference): app contracts, commands, configuration, and compatibility.
- [Explanation](https://daybrite.dev/docs/explanation): framework concepts for app developers.
- [Contributing](https://daybrite.dev/contributing): framework setup, architecture, backend contracts, documentation standards, and history.

Repository documents remain canonical in `docs/`; public routes are recorded in
`website/src/data/content-routes.json`. Source paths do not determine the public route.


## Invariants (for code generation)

- Build once, bind forever — never rebuild the view on state change; bind a Signal instead.
- `Signal<T>` is `Copy` — move it into closures directly; never wrap it in `Rc`/`Arc`.
- Containers take a tuple of children: `column((a, b, c))`; end a heterogeneous Piece with `.any()`.
- Edit `Day.toml` and Rust; never hand-edit generated Xcode/Gradle scaffolds.
- Verify on a real target with `day launch -t <target>`; `cargo build` alone does not prove a target works.
